summary: Defines a URL scheme for pointing to objects on an IMAP server, such as mailboxes or messages. It obsoletes RFC 2192 and updates RFC 4467. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: This is a way to write a web-style link that points to a particular email folder or message on a mail server.

questions: how to link to an imap message
what is the default imap port in a url
subtitle: How to write a link that points at an IMAP server, a mailbox, a search result or a single message.

tldr.problem: IMAP gives access to remote message stores, but there was no standard way to write a link that refers to a server, mailbox, message or message part.
tldr.mechanism: The imap: URL scheme encodes the server, optional user and authentication mechanism, mailbox, search, message UID, section and byte range. An optional URLAUTH component adds an expiry and a token that grants access.
tldr.outcome: It obsoletes RFC 2192 and updates RFC 4467. Clients must take care before sending credentials to a server named in a URL.

today: RFC 5092 is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes RFC 2192 and updates RFC 4467. It has itself been updated by RFC 5593, and has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: The IMAP URL Forms
sections.content:
The IMAP URL scheme designates IMAP servers, mailboxes, messages, MIME bodies and search programs on hosts reachable over IMAP and TCP. It follows the generic URI syntax, and if the port is left out it defaults to 143.

There are three absolute forms. imap://<iserver>/ names a server. imap://<iserver>/<enc-mailbox>[<uidvalidity>][?<enc-search>] names a mailbox or the messages matching a search. The last form adds a message UID, and optionally a section, a byte range and a URLAUTH part, to name one message or part of it.

The server part is [iuserinfo "@"] host [":" port]. The ABNF in Section 11 of the RFC is normative where it differs from the looser syntax shown earlier.
sections.eli5: The link has an address for the mail server, then a folder, then optionally one letter in that folder.

sections.title: User Names and Authentication
sections.content:
The userinfo part holds an optional user name and an optional authentication mechanism written as ;AUTH=<mechanism>. The user name also sets the mailbox naming scope. Without one, the URL can only refer to globally unique mailbox names. For example, imap://michael@example.org/INBOX is most likely a different mailbox from imap://bester@example.org/INBOX.

With no user name and no mechanism, the client MUST authenticate as anonymous. If the server advertises AUTH=ANONYMOUS, the client MUST use SASL ANONYMOUS. Otherwise it uses LOGIN with the user name anonymous and the user's email address as the password, but never when the server advertises LOGINDISABLED.

The string ;AUTH=* tells the client to pick a suitable mechanism, which lets one URL give read-write access to authorized users and read-only anonymous access to others. A user name with no mechanism means ;AUTH=*. The asterisk MUST NOT be percent-encoded here.

Because the same user field both sets the naming scope and limits who can resolve the URL, a URL with a user name can be resolved only by that owner. The RFC advises using globally unique mailbox names whenever possible.
sections.eli5: The link can say who you are and how to prove it. If it does not, you walk in as a guest.

sections.title: Mailboxes, Searches and Messages
sections.content:
For a mailbox, the enc-mailbox is used as the argument to IMAP SELECT or EXAMINE. The optional ;UIDVALIDITY= field MUST equal the mailbox's UIDVALIDITY value when the URL was made, so the program can tell if the URL is stale. A stale URL is treated as if the mailbox does not exist. A ? query is used as arguments to the IMAP SEARCH command. Quoted strings and non-synchronizing literals are allowed in it, but synchronizing literals are not.

For a message, ;UID= gives the message's unique identifier, used with UID FETCH. An optional ;SECTION= selects a part, as in BODY.PEEK[section]. An optional ;PARTIAL= selects a byte range, written as an offset and an optional length.

Unsafe or reserved characters such as space, ; or ? MUST be percent-encoded.
sections.eli5: After the server name, the link names a folder, then maybe a search, or the number of one message, or just a piece of that message.

sections.title: URLAUTH Authorized URLs
sections.content:
If the server advertises the URLAUTH capability, a message or part URL can carry URLAUTH, which conveys permission to read the data. It has an access identifier, an authorization mechanism name and an authorization token. The token is derived from the URL, the identifier, the mechanism and a secret mailbox access key. That key is random with at least 128 bits of entropy, generated by software or hardware rather than a person, and kept per user and per mailbox.

The form is ;URLAUTH=<access>:<mech>:<token>, and it MUST be at the end of the URL. An optional ;EXPIRE=<datetime> sets the latest valid time, after which servers MUST reject the URL. Without it the URL does not expire, but can be revoked with the RESETKEY command. The token is an ASCII hexadecimal string of at least 128 bits, so at least 32 hexadecimal digits.

The access identifier limits who may use it:

  • submit+userid: only a session authorized as a message submission entity for that user.
  • user+userid: only sessions logged in as that user.
  • authuser: any authenticated, non-anonymous session.
  • anonymous: any session, including anonymous ones.
sections.eli5: A special link can carry a secret code, like a ticket, that lets the holder open one email. The ticket can expire, and some tickets work only for certain people.

sections.title: Relative URLs and Internationalization
sections.content:
Relative IMAP URLs resolve by the generic URI rules, and parameters such as ;uid= and ;section= count as part of the path. The authentication part is treated as part of the user name, so a relative URL inherits the mechanism from the base URL unless it names a new user and server. Relative-path references (those not starting with a slash) MUST NOT be generated or accepted.

URLs always use / as the hierarchy delimiter, so relative mailbox paths only work if the mailbox uses /. Mailbox names that look like dot-segments, or start with a slash, MUST be percent-encoded.

IMAP's modified UTF-7 mailbox encoding MUST be converted to UTF-8, and the octets percent-encoded. User names and 8-bit search text are likewise percent-encoded. Appendix A gives sample C code for the mailbox conversion.
sections.eli5: A short link such as "the same folder, message 20" works from a full link. Letters from other languages are written in a safe code so every program reads them the same way.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
URLs can come from untrusted sources, and handing credentials to the wrong server may compromise an account. A client resolving a URL that needs authentication should meet one of five conditions: the URL comes from a trusted source, local site policy allows the server, the user confirms, a mechanism validates the server first (such as DIGEST-MD5 with mutual authentication), or the mechanism reveals nothing reusable (such as ANONYMOUS or GSSAPI).

Clients that store plaintext passwords MUST NOT use one for an IMAP URL without the user's explicit permission to supply it to that host. Clients wanting confidentiality or integrity SHOULD use STARTTLS before authenticating, or a SASL mechanism with a confidentiality layer. A URL with ;AUTH=* needs extra care because it might fall back on a weaker mechanism.

For URLAUTH, user+ and submit+ limit use to suitably authenticated sessions. authuser and anonymous do not, so authuser should only cover content any authorized user may see and anonymous only content anyone may see.
sections.eli5: A link can trick you into giving your password to the wrong place. So the program should check where it is going before it hands over any secrets.

viz.caption: AN IMAP URL AND THE COMMANDS IT MAY LEAD TO (FROM RFC 5092 EXAMPLES, ABRIDGED)

data.title: Message URL and client commands
data.code:
imap://;AUTH=GSSAPI@minbari.example.org/gray-council/;uid=20/;section=1.2

<connect to minbari.example.org, port 143>
C: A000 CAPABILITY
S: * CAPABILITY IMAP4rev1 STARTTLS AUTH=GSSAPI
C: A001 AUTHENTICATE GSSAPI
C: A002 SELECT gray-council
C: A003 UID FETCH 20 BODY.PEEK[1.2]
